google-ads.name: Google Ads
google-ads.summary: Show up on Google Search and Maps the moment someone needs you.

meta.title: Google Ads management for local businesses
meta.description: Google Search and Maps ads for service businesses: set up around searches that turn into jobs, with every call and lead tracked. Month to month.

hero.title: Google Ads that bring calls, not just clicks
hero.description: When someone searches for a plumber, a dentist or a roofer near them, your ad shows up first. I set up and run the campaigns, and every call and form is tracked so you see what each job cost.

intro.heading: Paying for clicks that never call?
paragraphs: Most local Google Ads accounts waste money the same way: broad keywords, no negative keywords, ads running at 3 AM and no idea which click turned into a customer.
I build the account around the searches that actually turn into work in your area, cut the rest, and measure calls and leads, not impressions. You own the account from day one.

details.heading: How I run Google Ads for local service businesses

sections.title: Keywords that turn into jobs
paragraphs: Not every search is worth paying for. "Emergency plumber near me" is someone with water on the floor right now; "how to fix a leaky faucet" is someone who wants to do it themselves. I build campaigns around searches with intent to call, and exclude searches for tips, jobs and free fixes from day one.
I use tight match types and a negative keyword list that grows every week from the real search terms that triggered clicks. Your budget goes to people looking for your service, in your service area.

sections.title: Search, Maps and click-to-call
paragraphs: For local businesses, Google Search and Google Maps ads bring the most calls. I link Google Ads to your Google Business Profile, so your ad also shows on the map with your address, rating and a call button.
I add call, sitelink, callout and location assets, so the ad takes more space, answers more questions and lets people call you without visiting the site.

sections.title: Tracking: what each lead costs
paragraphs: I set up conversion tracking with Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics 4: calls from ads, clicks on your phone number, WhatsApp messages and form submissions. Every lead shows in the report, so you know your real cost per lead, not just clicks.
Based on that data I adjust bids, ad schedule and budget by campaign. Money moves to what brings calls and stops where it doesn't.

faq.question: How much should I spend on Google Ads?
faq.answer: It depends on your trade and your area. In the free consultation I estimate what a click and a lead cost in your market, so you start with a budget that can actually bring jobs.

faq.question: How fast will I see results?
faq.answer: Ads can bring calls in the first days. The first month is about learning which searches turn into customers, and from the second month the cost per lead usually drops.

faq.question: Who owns the Google Ads account?
faq.answer: You do. The account and the billing are in your name, and I get manager access. If we stop working together, everything stays with you.

faq.question: Is there a long-term contract?
faq.answer: No. Management runs month to month and you can stop with a month's notice.

faq.question: Google Ads or SEO, which is better?
faq.answer: Google Ads brings calls right away; SEO builds steady traffic you don't pay for per click. The best order is usually ads first while SEO ramps up, then shift or lower the ad budget.

faq.question: Can you take over my existing Google Ads account?
faq.answer: Yes. I review it for free first, tell you what's broken and what's worth keeping, and we continue in the same account so you keep its history.

intro.heading: Boosting posts is not a strategy
paragraphs: The Boost button spends your money on likes. Likes don't book jobs.
I run lead campaigns with the Meta pixel and conversion tracking set up properly, aimed at your service area, with offers and creative tested against each other. You see what each lead cost.

details.heading: What Meta ads that bring leads look like

sections.title: Lead campaigns, not engagement
paragraphs: In Meta Ads Manager I pick the Leads or Sales objective, not Engagement. The algorithm then looks for people who send enquiries and call, not people who just like posts.

Leads can come through instant forms on Facebook and Instagram, through WhatsApp or Messenger, or from a page on your site. I choose the path that suits your customers and that you can follow up on easily.

sections.title: Location targeting and retargeting
paragraphs: Ads are shown to people who live in or move around the towns you serve. There's no point paying for impressions in a city you don't drive to.
Retargeting brings back people who visited your site, watched a video or opened a form without sending it. Those are your cheapest leads, because they already know you.

sections.title: Meta pixel and Conversions API
paragraphs: Without proper tracking, Meta doesn't know who became a customer. I set up the Meta pixel and the Conversions API, check the events and connect them to the enquiries from your site.
The platform learns from real leads, and you see in the report what each lead from Facebook and Instagram cost.

faq.question: Facebook ads or Google Ads, which is better?
faq.answer: Google catches people who are already searching. Facebook and Instagram reach people before they search and bring back the ones who visited. For most local businesses Google comes first and Meta helps it.

faq.question: Do I need to post every day?
faq.answer: No. Ads work without daily posting. A few good photos or short videos of your work are enough to start.

faq.question: What budget do I need?

faq.question: Do you make the images and videos?
faq.answer: I write the ad copy and build simple creatives from your photos. Real photos of your work shot on a phone usually beat stock images, because people trust real jobs.

faq.question: Do I need a Facebook page or Instagram account?

meta.title: Local SEO and Google Business Profile
meta.description: Local SEO for service businesses: Google Business Profile, reviews, a page for every service and town, and technical SEO, so you show up in the map pack.

hero.title: Local SEO that gets you into the Google map pack
hero.description: The three businesses on the map get most of the calls. I work on your Google Business Profile, reviews and website so you're one of them, in every town you serve.

intro.heading: Customers who find you without an ad
paragraphs: Ads stop when the budget stops. Local SEO keeps working: once you rank for "your service + your town", the calls keep coming without a cost per click.
It takes a few months, so I do it in order: first the Google Business Profile and the website basics, then a page for every service and every area, then reviews and links that build trust.

sections.title: Google Business Profile as the foundation
paragraphs: For searches like "roofer near me" or "dentist in [city]", Google shows a map with three businesses first. Your Google Business Profile drives most of that: the right primary category, secondary categories, services with descriptions, hours, photos and regular posts.
I set up the profile so your name, address and phone match the website, every service has a keyword-rich description, and posts link to the matching pages on your site.

sections.title: A page for every service and service area
paragraphs: One home page can't rank for everything you do. I build a separate page for each service, and where it makes sense for each town you serve, with unique copy, title and description.
The pages link to each other and to your Google Business Profile, and carry structured data (schema.org) so Google knows exactly what you offer and where.

sections.title: Reviews, citations and technical SEO
paragraphs: Reviews are one of the strongest local ranking signals. I give you a short link and a message to send happy customers, and every review gets a reply.

I check and build citations in the directories that matter (Apple Maps, Bing Places, Yelp and industry sites) with consistent details, and fix technical SEO: page speed, mobile layout, sitemap, Google Search Console indexing and canonical tags.

faq.question: How long does local SEO take?
faq.answer: The first changes on the map often show in a few weeks. Stable rankings for the main searches usually take three to six months, depending on competition.

faq.question: Do I need a website for local SEO?
faq.answer: A Google Business Profile alone can rank, but a fast site with a page for each service ranks better and turns more visitors into calls.

faq.question: Can you guarantee first place?
faq.answer: No one honest can. I can show you what I'm doing each month and how rankings, calls and enquiries change.

faq.question: How much does local SEO cost?
faq.answer: It depends on the number of services, locations and how competitive your market is. After the free consultation you get a flat monthly price with no long-term contract.

faq.question: What is a Google Business Profile and do I need one?
faq.answer: It's your free business listing on Google Search and Maps, with address, phone, hours and reviews. Every local business needs one, because without it you can't show up on the map.

faq.question: Can you do SEO on a site you didn't build?
faq.answer: Yes. I review the site first and tell you what can be fixed in place and what would be cheaper to rebuild.

hero.title: Be the business ChatGPT recommends
hero.description: More people ask ChatGPT or Google's AI who to hire instead of scrolling through results. I make sure the answer includes you, with the right facts about what you do and where.

intro.heading: A new place where customers ask
paragraphs: AI assistants recommend businesses they can understand and verify: clear service pages, consistent details across the web and reviews that say what you're good at.
This work is called generative engine optimization (GEO). It builds on good SEO, so the same work helps you in Google too.

details.heading: How AI search decides who to recommend

sections.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews
paragraphs: When someone asks ChatGPT "who's a good HVAC company near me" or Google shows an AI Overview above the results, the answer is built from sources the model trusts: business websites, Google Business Profiles, reviews, directories and articles.
If the facts about your business are clear and consistent everywhere, the model is more likely to mention you. If they're vague or contradict each other, it recommends someone else.

sections.title: Content AI can quote
paragraphs: I write pages that answer customer questions directly: what you do, where, for whom, how long it takes and roughly what it costs. Short, clear answers and real facts are what AI models quote most.
I add structured data (schema.org for the business, services and FAQs) and an llms.txt file, a site map written for AI crawlers.

sections.title: Mentions beyond your website
paragraphs: AI models trust a business that others mention too: local news, directories, associations and reviews. I work on getting your business listed in those places with the same name and description.
Every month I check what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity answer to your customers' questions and record whether you appear.

faq.question: Is AI search really used for finding local businesses?
faq.answer: More and more. Google already shows AI answers above the results, and many people ask ChatGPT for recommendations directly.

faq.question: Is this different from SEO?
faq.answer: It builds on SEO. AI answers rely on clear, consistent and well-reviewed information, so the work helps both.

faq.question: Can you make ChatGPT always recommend me?
faq.answer: No one controls the answers. What I can do is give AI models every reason to name you and measure how often they do.

faq.question: What is GEO?
faq.answer: GEO (generative engine optimization) means optimizing your content and business data so AI assistants like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity mention and recommend you in their answers.

faq.question: How fast do results show in AI search?
faq.answer: Google AI Overviews react faster, often within weeks. Models like ChatGPT refresh less often, so some changes take a few months.

intro.heading: The first to reply gets the job
paragraphs: Most people contact two or three businesses and go with whoever answers first. A slow reply loses jobs you already paid to get.

details.heading: How an AI chat assistant works for a service business

sections.title: Answers in seconds, 24/7
paragraphs: The AI chat assistant on your site replies instantly, even at midnight on a Sunday. It handles the common questions: what services you offer, which areas you cover, rough prices and when you can come out.
Where it makes sense, the same assistant answers on WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger, so you don't have to hold your phone all day.

sections.title: From conversation to a ready lead
paragraphs: The assistant doesn't just chat. It collects what you need to quote the job: name, phone, address, a description of the work and a photo if needed.

sections.title: Safe and under your control

hero.title: Privacy Policy
hero.description: What data I collect, why, for how long, and what your rights are.

privacy.intro: This policy explains how stojanpetkovic.com processes personal data, in line with the Serbian Law on Personal Data Protection and, where it applies, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

sections.title: 1. Controller
paragraphs: The controller is Stojan Petkovic, Zrenjanin, Serbia. Contact for any question about your data: {email}.

sections.title: 2. What I collect
items: Form data (contact and free consultation): name, email, phone, website address, business and location, your answers and your message.

Visit data, without cookies: which pages were opened, where the visitor came from (search, ad or link) and whether they tapped the phone number or WhatsApp or sent a form. This is not linked to your name unless you send a form.
Technical data logged by the server: IP address, browser type and time of access, for security and to run the site.
Analytics and advertising cookies (Google, Meta), only if you allow them in the cookie banner.

sections.title: 3. Why, and on what basis
items: To answer your enquiry and prepare a proposal: steps before a contract, at your request.
To deliver contracted work and keep required records: contract and legal obligation.
To measure which pages and sources bring enquiries and to keep the site secure: legitimate interest.
Analytics and ad measurement through cookies: your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
I do not sell data, send newsletters or use it for automated decision-making.

sections.title: 4. Who receives the data
paragraphs: Data is processed by services acting for me as processors, only for the purposes in this policy:
items: Vercel: website hosting.
webtano.com: the system where form enquiries arrive and are stored.
Resend: email notifications about enquiries.
Google (Analytics, Ads) and Meta (Facebook, Instagram): only if you allow those cookies.
Public authorities, only where the law requires it.

sections.title: 5. Transfers outside Serbia
paragraphs: Some of these services store data in the European Union or the United States. Transfers rely on the safeguards the law provides, such as standard contractual clauses or adequacy decisions.

sections.title: 6. How long
items: Enquiries: as long as needed to reply and make a proposal, and at most two years after the last contact.
Client data and invoices: as long as the law requires.
Cookieless visit data: in aggregate, without a time limit, as it does not relate to an identifiable person.
Cookies: for the period shown in the cookie settings.

sections.title: 7. Cookies
paragraphs: Necessary cookies keep the site working and remember your choice in the banner. Analytics and advertising cookies are set only with your consent. You can change your choice at any time in the cookie settings at the foot of the page.

sections.title: 8. Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict processing and to data portability, to object to processing based on legitimate interest, and to withdraw consent without affecting earlier processing. Send requests to {email}; I reply within 30 days.
You can complain to the Serbian Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection (www.poverenik.rs) or to the supervisory authority of the EU country where you live.

sections.title: 9. Security
paragraphs: The site runs over HTTPS, access to enquiries is password-protected and limited to me, and the services I use apply technical and organisational safeguards.

sections.title: 10. Changes
paragraphs: I may change this policy when the processing changes. The date of the last change is shown at the top.
